html:
Two strong earthquakes that struck the Levant in October and November 1759, when the region was part of the Ottoman Empire.

The first, on 30 October, hit hardest around Safed in Galilee. The second, on 25 November, was larger and was felt over a wide area. It brought down buildings in Damascus and towns of the Beqaa Valley in today's Lebanon, and many people died, though the number is not known.

At Baalbek several of the great columns of the Roman temple of Jupiter fell, leaving the six that tourists see today. Damage is also recorded from Acre to Beirut and Tripoli.

Both shocks came from the Dead Sea Transform, the fault line that runs from the Red Sea north through the Jordan valley and Lebanon. Along with the 1202 Syria earthquake, they are among the largest known in the region's long written record.
sum: Two strong earthquakes that struck the Levant in October and November 1759, when the region was part of the Ottoman Empire.
